title: Revelation 12 — The woman clothed with the sun + the dragon cast down

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Primary uncial witnesses for Revelation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) and Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), with Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04) and P47/P115 where extant; Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does not contain Revelation in its original hand. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine/Textus Receptus tradition are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation).

citations: A. Yarbro Collins, The Combat Myth in the Book of Revelation (1976)
verdicts.reasoning: sēmeion mega ōphthē en tō ouranō, gynē peribeblēmenē ton hēlion ... stephanos asterōn dōdeka. Exact; identifications of the woman correctly kept out of the line.
en gastri echousa; kai krazei ōdinousa kai basanizomenē tekein. Present kept; exact.

drakōn megas pyrros, echōn kephalas hepta kai kerata deka kai epi tas kephalas autou hepta diadēmata. 'fiery red' matches 6:4; diadēma/stephanos distinction noted; Lôtanu central entry left as background.
hē oura autou syrei (present) ... kai ebalen (aorist) ...; ho drakōn hestēken enōpion tēs gynaikos ... hina hotan tekē to teknon autēs kataphagē. Tense mix kept; exact.

citations: Ps 2:9 LXX (poimaneis autous en rhabdō sidēra)
verdicts.reasoning: eteken huion, arsen (neuter solecism noted), hos mellei poimainein panta ta ethnē en rhabdō sidēra: 'rule' with the rod of iron (all versions) vs 'be their shepherd' at 7:17 is a defensible context split; hērpasthē 'was caught up'.
ephygen eis tēn erēmon, hopou echei ekei topon hētoimasmenon apo tou theou, hina ekei trephōsin autēn hēmeras 1260. Indefinite plural and apo-agent noted. Exact.
ho Michaēl kai hoi angeloi autou tou polemēsai meta tou drakontos: nominative + articular infinitive rendered 'fighting against'. Defensible and standard.
kai ouk ischysen, oude topos heurethē autōn eti en tō ouranō. Singular verb (dragon) noted; exact.

ho drakōn ho megas, ho ophis ho archaios, ho kaloumenos Diabolos kai ho Satanas: after ho kaloumenos both function as names, so 'the Devil and Satan' (ASV) is correct; central ha-satan ('the adversary') correctly not applied to the Greek.

Arti egeneto hē sōtēria kai hē dynamis kai hē basileia tou theou hēmōn kai hē exousia tou christou autou ... ho katēgōr. 'power' (dynamis) vs 'authority' (exousia) kept distinct per overlay; 'his Christ' per central christos. Exact.
enikēsan auton dia to haima tou arniou ... ouk ēgapēsan tēn psychēn autōn achri thanatou: 'by' for dia + acc. (ASV 'because of'), 'their life' (ASV). Defensible.

citations: SBLGNT (variant marker at tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan)

Exact; TR tois katoikousi correctly reported; 'the devil' lower case in running text as ASV. Reception note (Satan's last opportunity) verified; no leakage.
hote eiden ho drakōn hoti eblēthē ... ediōxen tēn gynaika hētis eteken ton arsena. 'persecuted' (ASV) with 'pursue' sense noted. Exact.
edothēsan tē gynaiki hai dyo pteryges tou aetou tou megalou ... kairon kai kairous kai hēmisy kairou apo prosōpou tou opheōs. Exact.
ebalen ho ophis ... opisō tēs gynaikos hydōr hōs potamon, hina autēn potamophorēton poiēsē. Exact.
eboēthēsen hē gē tē gynaiki ... ēnoixen hē gē to stoma autēs kai katepien ton potamon. Exact.

citations: SBLGNT (no variant marker: Robinson-Pierpont also reads Iēsou alone)
verdicts.reasoning: ōrgisthē ... apēlthen poiēsai polemon meta tōn loipōn tou spermatos autēs ... tēn martyrian Iēsou. Exact; TR Christou correctly attributed to the TR.

Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament (2nd ed. 1994)
glossaryReview.reasoning: claim_type direct is right: the entry declares which text is translated and how variants are reported. Three accuracy fixes. (1) The 8:7 omission is a Textus Receptus (minority) reading, not that of the Byzantine majority text, which the SBLGNT apparatus shows agreeing with SBLGNT; rephrase wherever 'Byzantine' is said there. (2) Add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou, quoted by the canon's English) to the wohChoice list of KJV-wording variants, and 16:18 (NA28 singular anthrōpos egeneto; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'). (3) Add REV-WOH-16:18's NA28 divergence to the 'NA28 bracketed or divergent readings reported' sentence. The decision itself stands.

citations: LXX usage: kyrios for the Tetragrammaton, theos for ʾĕlōhîm
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct: theos never renders the Tetragrammaton in the LXX or NT, the canon's French reads 'Dieu' at every site, and published chapters 1, 4, 6 use 'God'. The canon's English 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' is recorded in reception notes without entering the line.

citations: BDAG s.vv. diabolos, Satanas, Abaddōn, Harmagedōn
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct for a presentation and scope convention. Recommendation (non-blocking): state the scope criterion explicitly. Hebrew-text central entries are applied to a Greek line when their English choice is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme (chayyot 'living creatures' at 7:11; gophrit 'sulfur' for theion). They are background only where applying them would import a Hebrew-specific form or sense (Yisra'el, 'the adversary', 'the deep'). Without that sentence the 7:11 chayyot ref and the gophrit extension look like exceptions to rule (4).

Direct is defensible: BDAG separates the capability and jurisdiction senses, Revelation sets dynamis beside exousia at 13:2, and exousia epi + accusative is uniformly 'authority over' (6:8, 13:7, 16:9). The 16:9 line change follows the construction, not the lens.

Direct is defensible: at 8:9 and 16:3 the psychai are sea creatures, and psychē zōēs reproduces nep̄eš ḥayyâ. 'every living being' matches RSV/NRSV in sense. Non-blocking: the 16:3 TR variant zōsa (KJV 'every living soul') could be named in the rationale.
Direct is defensible: 'tabernacle' keeps the Lev 26/Ezek 37 allusion at 21:3, 'dwell' is universal for the verb, and the 7:15 ASV exception is grammatically motivated by epi + accusative.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line was checked: all 146 lines, and specifically the 21 reception-note sites (7:3, 8:1, 8:7, 8:8, 8:10, 8:12, 9:1, 9:5, 9:9, 9:13, 9:18, 10:4, 10:7, 12:12, 13:18, 16:18, 16:20, 16:21, 21:1, 21:2, 21:3). A script found no Elohim, Yahweh, YHWH, craft, missile, atomic, nuclear, planet, Eternals, loudspeaker or similar lens vocabulary in any line. The only hits were 'ship(s)' (8:9 ploia; worship) and 'Israel' (substring 'rael'), both benign. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own headed paragraph labelled 'reception note, not a translation claim'. Each was verified against LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:155-228), FR and EN. No line resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction: the visionary hōs/homoios markers are kept (8:8; 9:7-10), 'the number of a man' stays open (13:18), 'breastplates' is used rather than the canon's French 'thorax' (9:9), 'pit of the abyss' is kept (9:1), and theos is 'God' where the canon's English has 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' (9:13; 21:2-4). Where the line and the canon's English diverge, the line follows the Greek critical text, and at 8:7 that text agrees with the canon's French.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 146 verses, the 10 overlay entries touched and the 13 diff ops were formed from the chapters, the SBLGNT sources (including the sigla-bearing Rev.txt in the scratchpad), the overlay, the diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-r2-editor-report.md. After reading the report, no verdict changed. The report's Founder point C lists the KJV-wording variants named in commentary (8:7, 9:13, 10:4, 21:2, 21:3 'his people ... their God', 21:4). It omits 21:3 'out of heaven', which confirms the reviewer's 21:3 revise. Its 9:13 request ('the Reviewer should verify this against the NA28 apparatus') was met as far as possible: the SBLGNT marker confirms a collated edition reads tessarōn, and the corrected attribution agrees with the reviewer's reading of Metzger. The printed NA28 apparatus was not available, so this is recorded as unverified at the sigla level, not as a defect. The report's 'All other lines are the Translator's draft, unchanged' was confirmed by diffing against the rev_r2 backup: only 16:3 and 16:9 differ.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-theion-sulfur: Endorse. LXX theion = gophrit (Gen 19:24), BDAG 'sulfur', NRSV 'sulfur' at all four sites; the central entry already renders the Revelation lake passages 'sulfur'. The canon's English 'brimstone' (9:18) is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-theos-God-not-Yahweh-Elohim: Endorse firmly. theos does not render the Tetragrammaton, the canon's own French has 'Dieu', and chapters 1, 4, 6 are signed off with 'God'. Writing 'Yahweh' would translate the canon's English edition, not the Greek.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-critical-text-over-KJV-wording: Endorse. Complete the inventory: add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou) and 16:18 (NA28 singular; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'); correct 8:7 to say the omission is a TR reading, not the Byzantine majority's. Optionally name 16:3 zōsa and 21:4 hoti.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-names-and-scope-rule: Endorse, and support promotion to a central Greek-NT convention. Add the explicit criterion (apply where the central English is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme; background where it imports a Hebrew-specific form), which explains chayyot at 7:11 and gophrit for theion.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-exousia: Endorse. The context rule follows BDAG's sense division and RSV/NRSV practice; 16:9 'authority over' aligns with 6:8 and 13:7. Uniform 'authority' would read badly at 9:10, 19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-16:3-living-being: Endorse. 'soul' for sea creatures imports a personal sense; 'living being' keeps the noun and the nep̄eš ḥayyâ echo.
founderDecisionRecommendations.G-doulos-servants: Endorse. Keeps the signed-off 1:1/6:11 and the canon's English 'servants'; the French 'esclaves' is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.H-pit-of-the-abyss: Endorse. ASV structure; matches the canon's French 'le puits de l'abîme'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.I-Har-magedon: Endorse. ASV form, follows the SBLGNT/NA28 rough breathing, keeps har visible without deciding the etymology.
founderDecisionRecommendations.J-12:18-versification: Endorse. P47, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read estathē, and SBLGNT/NA28 number it 12:18 (Metzger on 12:18). The ASV 13:1a alignment is a tooling task (orchestrator follow-up 2), not a translation issue.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα,
paragraphs.translit: kai sēmeion mega ōphthē en tō ouranō, gynē peribeblēmenē ton hēlion, kai hē selēnē hypokatō tōn podōn autēs, kai epi tēs kephalēs autēs stephanos asterōn dōdeka,

i18n.en: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars;

notes.official: *sēmeion mega ōphthē en tō ouranō* 'a great sign appeared in heaven': *sēmeion* is a portent, the first of three signs 'in heaven' (12:3; 15:1), and *ouranos* here is the sky as the stage of the vision. *gynē peribeblēmenē ton hēlion, kai hē selēnē hypokatō tōn podōn autēs, kai epi tēs kephalēs autēs stephanos asterōn dōdeka* 'a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars'. The imagery draws on Joseph's dream of sun, moon and stars (Gen 37:9), on Zion as a woman in labour (Isa 26:17; 66:7-9; Mic 4:10), and on the Greco-Roman myth of a pregnant goddess pursued by a dragon (Leto and Python; cf. Isis and Typhon) (A. Yarbro Collins, *The Combat Myth in the Book of Revelation*, 1976). The identifications of the woman (Israel, the people of God, Mary, the church) are interpretations and are not built into the line.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα· καὶ κράζει ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai en gastri echousa· kai krazei ōdinousa kai basanizomenē tekein.

i18n.en: and she was with child; and she cries out in birth pains, in agony to give birth.

notes.official: *en gastri echousa* 'with child' (idiom). *kai krazei* 'and she cries out': the present tense is kept. *ōdinousa kai basanizomenē tekein* 'in birth pains, in agony to give birth'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἰδοὺ δράκων μέγας πυρρός, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα,
paragraphs.translit: kai ōphthē allo sēmeion en tō ouranō, kai idou drakōn megas pyrros, echōn kephalas hepta kai kerata deka kai epi tas kephalas autou hepta diadēmata,

i18n.en: And another sign appeared in heaven; and behold, a great fiery red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven diadems.

notes.official: *drakōn megas pyrros* 'a great fiery red dragon' (*pyrros* 'fiery red', as the horse of 6:4). *echōn kephalas hepta kai kerata deka* 'having seven heads and ten horns'. The Septuagint uses *drakōn* for Heb. *tannîn* and *liwyāṯān* (Isa 27:1; Ps 74:13-14), and the seven-headed sea monster is the Lôtanu of the Ugaritic Baal Cycle, collected in the central `lotanu-leviathan-seven-headed-serpent-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible` (background; the line keeps Greek *drakōn* 'dragon'). The ten horns are those of Daniel's fourth beast (Dan 7:7). *diadēmata* 'diadems' are royal bands, distinct from the *stephanos* 'crown' of v 1.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ αὐτοῦ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἕστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τεκεῖν, ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς καταφάγῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hē oura autou syrei to triton tōn asterōn tou ouranou, kai ebalen autous eis tēn gēn. kai ho drakōn hestēken enōpion tēs gynaikos tēs mellousēs tekein, hina hotan tekē to teknon autēs kataphagē.

i18n.en: And his tail sweeps away a third of the stars of heaven, and he cast them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child.

notes.official: *hē oura autou syrei to triton tōn asterōn tou ouranou* 'his tail sweeps away a third of the stars of heaven': from Dan 8:10, where the little horn casts some of the host and of the stars to the ground. The present *syrei* followed by the aorist *ebalen* is kept. *hina hotan tekē to teknon autēs kataphagē* 'so that when she gave birth he might devour her child' (cf. Jer 51:34, Babylon swallowing like a dragon).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ἄρσεν, ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eteken huion, arsen, hos mellei poimainein panta ta ethnē en rhabdō sidēra· kai hērpasthē to teknon autēs pros ton theon kai pros ton thronon autou.

i18n.en: And she gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron; and her child was caught up to God and to his throne.

notes.official: *eteken huion, arsen* 'she gave birth to a son, a male child': the neuter *arsen* in apposition to the masculine *huion* is a solecism, probably an echo of Isa 66:7 LXX (*eteken arsen*). *hos mellei poimainein panta ta ethnē en rhabdō sidēra* 'who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron' quotes Ps 2:9 in its Septuagint form (*poimaneis autous en rhabdō sidēra*), which read Heb. *tərōʿēm* 'you will break them' as *tirʿēm* 'you will shepherd them'. *poimainō* is 'shepherd', but with 'a rod of iron' the sense is governing, and 'rule' (ASV, KJV, RSV, NRSV) is kept; the same Psalm text recurs at 2:27 and 19:15. At 7:17, where the context is pastoral, the verb is 'be their shepherd'. *hērpasthē* 'was caught up' is the verb of rapture (2 Cor 12:2, 4; 1 Thess 4:17).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα ἐκεῖ τρέφωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: kai hē gynē ephygen eis tēn erēmon, hopou echei ekei topon hētoimasmenon apo tou theou, hina ekei trephōsin autēn hēmeras chilias diakosias hexēkonta.

i18n.en: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they may nourish her for a thousand two hundred and sixty days.

notes.official: *ephygen eis tēn erēmon* 'fled into the wilderness': the place of Israel's protection and provision after the exodus (Ex 16; Hos 2:14). *topon hētoimasmenon apo tou theou* 'a place prepared by God' (*apo* for the agent, instead of *hypo*). *hina ekei trephōsin autēn* 'so that there they may nourish her': indefinite plural. *hēmeras chilias diakosias hexēkonta* '1,260 days' are 42 months, three and a half years (11:2-3; 13:5), Daniel's 'time, times and half a time' (Dan 7:25; 12:7; v 14).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ τοῦ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τοῦ δράκοντος. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησεν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto polemos en tō ouranō, ho michaēl kai hoi angeloi autou tou polemēsai meta tou drakontos. kai ho drakōn epolemēsen kai hoi angeloi autou,

i18n.en: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fighting against the dragon. And the dragon and his angels fought,

notes.official: *ho Michaēl kai hoi angeloi autou tou polemēsai meta tou drakontos* 'Michael and his angels fighting against the dragon': a nominative subject with an articular infinitive is a Hebraism (Charles, ICC; Aune, WBC 52B). Michael is the 'great prince' who stands for Israel in Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1 (central `michael-as-israels-prince-angel-dan-10-13-21-12-1-cross-corpus`, which keeps 'Michael' as a proper noun). *polemos en tō ouranō* 'war in heaven'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν, οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη αὐτῶν ἔτι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk ischysen, oude topos heurethē autōn eti en tō ouranō.

i18n.en: and he did not prevail, nor was their place found any longer in heaven.

notes.official: *kai ouk ischysen* 'and he did not prevail': singular, the dragon. *oude topos heurethē autōn eti en tō ouranō* 'nor was their place found any longer in heaven': cf. Dan 2:35 (Th), 'no place was found for them'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐβλήθη ὁ δράκων ὁ μέγας, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην— ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐβλήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eblēthē ho drakōn ho megas, ho ophis ho archaios, ho kaloumenos diabolos kai ho satanas, ho planōn tēn oikoumenēn holēn— eblēthē eis tēn gēn, kai hoi angeloi autou metʼ autou eblēthēsan.

i18n.en: And the great dragon was cast down, the ancient serpent, who is called the Devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world; he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.

notes.official: *ho drakōn ho megas, ho ophis ho archaios* 'the great dragon, the ancient serpent' identifies the dragon with the serpent of Gen 3. *ho kaloumenos Diabolos kai ho Satanas* 'who is called the Devil and Satan': *diabolos* 'slanderer' is the Septuagint's rendering of Heb. *haśśāṭān* in Job 1-2 and Zech 3:1-2, and *Satanas* transliterates Aramaic *sāṭānā*. Introduced by 'who is called', both are names of one figure here, and the line keeps them as names (ASV). The central `ha-satan` ('the adversary') governs the Hebrew of Job, where the article marks a role; it is not applied to the Greek (`greek-nt-proper-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-revelation`). The forensic role survives in v 10 as *ho katēgōr* 'the accuser'. *ho planōn tēn oikoumenēn holēn* 'the deceiver of the whole world'. The Jewish traditions of a chief of evil spirits (Mastema in Jubilees and at Qumran; central `mastema-prince-of-evil-spirits-jubilees-10-cd-1qs-1qm-cross-corpus`) are background.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγουσαν· Ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐβλήθη ὁ κατήγωρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν, ὁ κατηγορῶν αὐτοὺς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousa phōnēn megalēn en tō ouranō legousan· arti egeneto hē sōtēria kai hē dynamis kai hē basileia tou theou hēmōn kai hē exousia tou christou autou, hoti eblēthē ho katēgōr tōn adelphōn hēmōn, ho katēgorōn autous enōpion tou theou hēmōn hēmeras kai nyktos.

i18n.en: And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying: "Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of his Christ, for the accuser of our brothers has been cast down, who accuses them before our God day and night.

notes.official: The hymn of vv 10-12 interprets the war. *Arti egeneto hē sōtēria kai hē dynamis kai hē basileia tou theou hēmōn* 'Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God'. *kai hē exousia tou christou autou* 'and the authority of his Christ': *christos* 'anointed' is the title of Ps 2:2 ('against YHWH and against his anointed'), kept as 'Christ' under the central `christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic`; *exousia* 'authority' (`exousia-authority-power-rendering-revelation`). *ho katēgōr tōn adelphōn hēmōn* 'the accuser of our brothers': *katēgōr* passed into rabbinic Hebrew as *qāṭêḡôr*, the prosecuting angel, and it is the court role of *haśśāṭān* in Job 1-2 and Zech 3:1 (central `ha-satan`, background). The speech runs to v 12.

paragraphs.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνίκησαν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου·
paragraphs.translit: kai autoi enikēsan auton dia to haima tou arniou kai dia ton logon tēs martyrias autōn, kai ouk ēgapēsan tēn psychēn autōn achri thanatou·

i18n.en: And they conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their life even unto death.

notes.official: *enikēsan auton dia to haima tou arniou* 'they conquered him by the blood of the Lamb': *dia* with the accusative, 'because of, on the ground of'. *ouk ēgapēsan tēn psychēn autōn achri thanatou* 'they did not love their life even unto death': *psychē* 'life' (`psyche-soul-life-living-being-rendering-revelation`).

paragraphs.text: διὰ τοῦτο εὐφραίνεσθε, οἱ οὐρανοὶ καὶ οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς σκηνοῦντες. οὐαὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, ὅτι κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν, εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto euphrainesthe, hoi ouranoi kai hoi en autois skēnountes. ouai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan, hoti katebē ho diabolos pros hymas, echōn thymon megan, eidōs hoti oligon kairon echei.

i18n.en: Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them! Woe to the earth and the sea, for the devil has come down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time."

notes.official:
*euphrainesthe, hoi ouranoi* 'rejoice, O heavens' (Isa 44:23; 49:13). *hoi en autois skēnountes* 'you who dwell in them': *skēnoō* 'dwell' (`skene-skenoo-tabernacle-dwell-rendering-revelation`). *ouai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan* 'Woe to the earth and the sea' is the reading of the SBLGNT and NA28; the Textus Receptus reads *ouai tois katoikousi tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan* (KJV 'Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea'). The line follows the SBLGNT (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). *ouai* with the accusative is peculiar to Revelation (8:13). *ho diabolos* 'the devil' is lower case in running text, as in the ASV and in Matthew (`greek-nt-proper-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-revelation`). *thymon megan* 'great wrath'; *oligon kairon* 'a short time'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes the second half of this verse (KJV wording, 'for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time') and reads the final test of humanity, the choice between self-destruction and the passage into the golden age, as Satan's last opportunity to prove that humanity is bad. The line keeps 'the devil' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ δράκων ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἐδίωξεν τὴν γυναῖκα ἥτις ἔτεκεν τὸν ἄρσενα.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote eiden ho drakōn hoti eblēthē eis tēn gēn, ediōxen tēn gynaika hētis eteken ton arsena.

i18n.en: And when the dragon saw that he had been cast down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who had given birth to the male child.

notes.official: *ediōxen* 'he persecuted': *diōkō* is both 'pursue' and 'persecute', and the flight of vv 14-16 brings out the first sense as well. *ton arsena* 'the male child' (v 5).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ αἱ δύο πτέρυγες τοῦ ἀετοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου, ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, ὅπου τρέφεται ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ ὄφεως.
paragraphs.translit: kai edothēsan tē gynaiki hai dyo pteryges tou aetou tou megalou, hina petētai eis tēn erēmon eis ton topon autēs, hopou trephetai ekei kairon kai kairous kai hēmisy kairou apo prosōpou tou opheōs.

i18n.en: And the two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.

notes.official: *hai dyo pteryges tou aetou tou megalou* 'the two wings of the great eagle': the exodus image of Ex 19:4 ('I bore you on eagles' wings') and Deut 32:11. *kairon kai kairous kai hēmisy kairou* 'a time and times and half a time': Dan 7:25 and 12:7, equal to the 1,260 days of v 6. *apo prosōpou tou opheōs* 'away from the face of the serpent' renders the Hebrew idiom *mippənê*.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω τῆς γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν, ἵνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ebalen ho ophis ek tou stomatos autou opisō tēs gynaikos hydōr hōs potamon, hina autēn potamophorēton poiēsē.

i18n.en: And the serpent cast water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, so that he might cause her to be carried away by the river.

notes.official: *hydōr hōs potamon* 'water like a river'; *potamophorēton* 'carried away by the river' is a rare word (BDAG). Floodwaters as an image of hostile powers: Ps 18:4; 124:2-5; Isa 43:2.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς καὶ κατέπιεν τὸν ποταμὸν ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai eboēthēsen hē gē tē gynaiki, kai ēnoixen hē gē to stoma autēs kai katepien ton potamon hon ebalen ho drakōn ek tou stomatos autou·

i18n.en: And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river that the dragon had cast out of his mouth.

notes.official: *ēnoixen hē gē to stoma autēs kai katepien* 'the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up': the formula of Num 16:30-32 (Korah) and Ex 15:12.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς, τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai ōrgisthē ho drakōn epi tē gynaiki, kai apēlthen poiēsai polemon meta tōn loipōn tou spermatos autēs, tōn tērountōn tas entolas tou theou kai echontōn tēn martyrian iēsou·

i18n.en: And the dragon was enraged at the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her seed, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus.

notes.official: *ōrgisthē ho drakōn epi tē gynaiki* 'the dragon was enraged at the woman'. *tōn loipōn tou spermatos autēs* 'the rest of her seed' recalls Gen 3:15, the enmity between the serpent and the woman's seed. *tēn martyrian Iēsou* 'the testimony of Jesus' is the reading of the SBLGNT and NA28; the Textus Receptus adds *Christou* (KJV 'of Jesus Christ'). The line follows the SBLGNT (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). 'Jesus' per the central `iēsous-yehoshua-yhwh-saves-folk-etymology-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης.
paragraphs.translit: kai estathē epi tēn ammon tēs thalassēs.

i18n.en: And he stood upon the sand of the sea.

notes.official: *kai estathē epi tēn ammon tēs thalassēs* 'And he stood upon the sand of the sea' is read by P47, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus and printed as 12:18 by the SBLGNT and NA28: the dragon takes his stand on the shore to summon the beast from the sea (13:1). The Textus Receptus reads *estathēn* 'I stood' and joins the clause to 13:1 (KJV 'And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast'). The ASV follows the better reading ('he stood') but prints it at the head of 13:1, so the ASV chapter has seventeen verses. The line follows the SBLGNT text and verse division (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`); in the ASV this clause is found at 13:1.
